messages:
anya: Quick sync — want to move lightfield-7b into the public model catalog. Need three quick confirmations: license clearance, perf profile (latency/cost at 2k/4k contexts), and owners for canary. TL;DR: model artifact is in GCS, ~72GB float32, we have a quantized checkpoint (8-bit) that passes unit tests but no perf sheet yet.

sam: I can own the canary and rollout. Question re infra: do we want sharded inference or single-node 80GB mem instance? Sharded means more infra work.

anya: @sam single-node would be simplest for initial canary but may not hit perf targets. If we can get 8-bit perf numbers on one node first that’s fine. If not, we fall back to sharded.

ram: On infra deps — current runtime has a sharding experimental flag. If we need sharding we should lock the runtime PR now. I can fast-track the PR but need owners to sign off on test matrix.

marco: Quick note on embeddings: model’s embedding head returns 1536-d floats, but our embedding pipeline expects 2048. I have a small adapter script but we need to decide whether to canonicalize shapes in catalog or add adapter. code:
```bash
# adapter prototype
python tools/embed_adapter.py --in-shape 1536 --out-shape 2048 --method pad
```
works but not ideal.

jules: License check: the repo lists 'BSD-3-Clause' but there's a third-party weights file with an additional non-commercial clause in weights/LICENSE.txt. I flagged it for legal review. Don’t ship until clarified.

legal-bot: Added to legal-review queue as LR-432. Expected turnaround ~48-72h unless priority bumped.

sam: Thanks Jules. If non-commercial clause exists we can still onboard as 'internal-only' for Dedicated/Private but not hosted. Need the exact text to decide options.

anya: Action items so far: 1) Jules/legal to confirm license by EOD+2; 2) Sam to run 8-bit perf numbers on single-node (canary) by Mon; 3) Marco to PR adapter or propose canonical shape; 4) Ram to prep sharding PR if perf needs it.

marco: I’ll open a PR for the adapter today (small change). If legal blocks hosted catalog, we can still include metadata in catalog with gated visibility.

ram: Sharding PR draft is here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1287 — marked WIP. I can finish tests if someone signs the test matrix.

sam: I’ll run perf this afternoon. Quick question: what sequence lengths should I target? 512/1024/2048?

anya: Start with 512 and 2048 (our common tails), and a 4k token run as worst-case. Capture p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.

jules: If legal confirms it's Apache or BSD-only, green to proceed. If NC clause present, I’ll propose the internal-only gating language and options for listing.

anya: Also: tagging for catalog metadata — add fields: "license_review_state", "embedding_shape", "canary_owner", "perf_profile_link". Keep the first draft minimal.

deploy-bot: canary-schedule created for sam on 2026-03-23T14:00Z (id: canary-3654).

sam: Got the schedule, I’ll ping infra when I start. If perf looks bad I’ll toggle sharding request.

anya: Final ask: drop a one-line status into this thread after each checklist item (license, perf, adapter pr, sharding pr). We’ll roll this into the catalog launch sweep on Friday.

marco: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-tools/pull/452 — adapter + tests.

sam: Perf runs done (512/2048/4096) — initial numbers look ok on 8-bit single-node for 512/2048, 4k is ~2x p95 which is borderline. Uploading perf sheet to: https://redwood.internal/sheets/lightfield7b-perf

ram: Noted. I’ll prioritize sharding test completion if 4k remains problematic.

jules: Legal: weight file contains 'non-commercial use only' clause. Need to escalate to licensing counsel — will update LR-432 once counsel responds.

anya: Thanks all. If counsel confirms NC clause, we’ll mark catalog entry as 'restricted' and notify product about hosting implications. Thread closed for async updates — keep one-line pings here.
